title: Architecture decision: monolith, SOA with an ESB, or microservices behind an API gateway
question: How should the Campus Event Planner connect Student Affairs, Finance and Facilities?
scale: Ratings: 1 = poor, 5 = very good. For simplicity, performance, skills and cost, 5 means simple, fast, familiar, cheap.
weightRule: A criterion's weight is the points of its NFR category (Must 3, Should 2, Could 1, see src/strategy.js and docs/nfr.json). Skills and cost are project constraints worth 3 points each.

criteria.name: Independent deployment
criteria.question: Can one system change without redeploying the others?

criteria.name: Fault isolation
criteria.question: When one part fails, do the other parts keep answering? (NFR-02)

criteria.name: Simplicity for a student team
criteria.question: How easy is it to understand, run and debug?

criteria.name: Performance overhead
criteria.question: How little time does the design add to a request? (NFR-01)

criteria.name: Team skills
criteria.question: Does the team already know the technology?

criteria.name: Cost
criteria.question: How cheap is it to build and to run for one semester?

options.name: Monolith
options.idea: One application holds all the code and one database.

deployment.why: every change redeploys the whole application

isolation.why: one crash or one slow module stops everything

simplicity.why: one project, one process, one debugger

performance.why: calls between modules are plain function calls

skills.why: students know one Express app, but not merging three systems

cost.why: one server, but the three existing systems must be migrated into it

options.name: SOA with an ESB
options.idea: Services talk through a central enterprise service bus that routes and transforms messages.

deployment.why: services deploy alone, but the bus configuration changes with them

isolation.why: the bus is a single point of failure for every call

simplicity.why: bus products and their configuration are heavy to learn

performance.why: every message is routed and transformed by the bus

skills.why: nobody in the team has used an ESB product

cost.why: licences or a big server, plus setup time

options.name: Microservices behind an API gateway
options.idea: Small services own their data and are reached through one thin gateway.

deployment.why: each service has its own process and release

isolation.why: timeouts and 502/504 keep one failure from spreading; the gateway itself is still one point

simplicity.why: more parts to start, but each part is small Express code

performance.why: one extra network hop per call

skills.why: Express and REST were learned in episode 9

cost.why: three small processes and a gateway: cheap, but more than one

context: The three systems already exist apart, with different owners and formats (the silos of episode 1). That is why the gateway design is considered at all.
